question: Since 28 September 2026, farmers and livestock breeders in Calabria have been protesting against the surge in fuel, energy and fertiliser costs, paltry producer prices and competition from imports. Calabria Region has set aside EUR 15 million. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1894 allocates EUR 45.

6 million in extraordinary aid to Italy and obliges the Member States to notify the Commission of criteria, beneficiaries and the forecast for payments by 30 September. Regulation (EU) 2026/1739 strengthens contractual relations in the agricultural sector, while a review of Directive (EU) 2019/633 has been announced. In light of the above: 1.

Did Italy notify the Commission of the measures taken under Regulation 2026/1894 by 30 September, and what allocation criteria, beneficiary sectors and payment timelines were communicated, including for holdings in Calabria?

In the revision of Directive 2019/633, does it intend to introduce a specific ban on practices that entail systematically selling below cost or any other contractual obligations, and by when will it present the proposal?

Does it consider EU rules on origin labelling and olive oil checks to be appropriate, and what action does it believe should be taken to address the competitive disadvantages stemming from differences in the production standards applied by imports?
